From ba2c83167b215da30fa2aae56b140198cf8d8408 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Xingjing Deng <micro6947@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 07:41:40 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] misc: fastrpc: possible double-free of cctx->remote_heap

fastrpc_init_create_static_process() may free cctx->remote_heap on the
err_map path but does not clear the pointer. Later, fastrpc_rpmsg_remove()
frees cctx->remote_heap again if it is non-NULL, which can lead to a
double-free if the INIT_CREATE_STATIC ioctl hits the error path and the rpmsg
device is subsequently removed/unbound.
Clear cctx->remote_heap after freeing it in the error path to prevent the
later cleanup from freeing it again.

This issue was found by an in-house analysis workflow that extracts AST-based
information and runs static checks, with LLM assistance for triage, and was
confirmed by manual code review.
No hardware testing was performed.

Fixes: 0871561055e66 ("misc: fastrpc: Add support for audiopd")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 6.2+
Signed-off-by: Xingjing Deng <xjdeng@buaa.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260129234140.410983-1-xjdeng@buaa.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/misc/fastrpc.c b/drivers/misc/fastrpc.c
index 47356a5d5804..19cfc487df7c 100644
--- a/drivers/misc/fastrpc.c
+++ b/drivers/misc/fastrpc.c
@@ -1401,6 +1401,7 @@ static int fastrpc_init_create_static_process(struct fastrpc_user *fl,
 	}
 err_map:
 	fastrpc_buf_free(fl->cctx->remote_heap);
+	fl->cctx->remote_heap = NULL;
 err_name:
 	kfree(name);
 err:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch addresses a double-free vulnerability in the `fastrpc` driver by adding a NULL assignment after freeing memory in an error path.

### File modified

**drivers/misc/fastrpc.c**

- **Function**: `fastrpc_init_create_static_process()`
- **Change**: Added `fl->cctx->remote_heap = NULL;` immediately after `fastrpc_buf_free(fl->cctx->remote_heap);` in the `err_map` error label.

### Relationship between modifications

The only modification is the single line that clears the pointer after freeing. This ensures that when the error path of `fastrpc_init_create_static_process()` frees `cctx->remote_heap`, the pointer is set to NULL. Consequently, if the rpmsg device is later removed (triggering `fastrpc_rpmsg_remove()`), the cleanup code will avoid a second free of the same memory because it checks for a non-NULL pointer before freeing. This prevents a double-free condition that could otherwise occur when the `INIT_CREATE_STATIC` ioctl fails and the device is subsequently unbound.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
fastrpc_buf_free(fl->cctx->remote_heap);  // in err_map of fastrpc_init_create_static_process
</text>
<text>
if (cctx->remote_heap) fastrpc_buf_free(cctx->remote_heap);  // in fastrpc_rpmsg_remove
</text>
Reason:
<text>
After fastrpc_buf_free in the err_map path, the pointer fl->cctx->remote_heap is not set to NULL. Later, when the rpmsg device is removed, fastrpc_rpmsg_remove checks if the pointer is non-NULL (it still holds the freed address) and frees it again, causing a double-free.
</text>
The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
fl->cctx->remote_heap = NULL;  // added after fastrpc_buf_free in err_map
</text>
Reason:
<text>
Setting the pointer to NULL immediately after freeing ensures that any subsequent check for non-NULL will skip the stale pointer, preventing the double-free in the cleanup path.
</text>
